questions.q: What happens when you read the first letter of every line in an acrostic poem vertically?
questions.a: The first letters spell out the subject word or phrase of the poem. A wrong answer suggests the student thinks the poem is read horizontally or doesn't understand the vertical structure.

questions.q: If you are writing an acrostic poem for the word "DANCE," why must every line relate to movement or rhythm?
questions.a: Because the lines must describe the topic to create a meaningful poem. A wrong answer shows the student treats it as a random word game rather than a form of creative expression.

questions.q: Write the first two lines of an acrostic poem using the word "SKY" to describe a sunny day.
questions.a: S: Sun shining bright above. K: Keeping the clouds away. A wrong answer often fails to start the line with the required letter or ignores the theme of a "sunny day."

questions.q: Analyze this poem: "B-Bright sun, R-Rain falls, A-All are happy." Is this a good acrostic poem for "BRAVE"? Why or why not?
questions.a: It is not a good acrostic because the lines do not describe being 'BRAVE'. A wrong answer suggests the student only cares about the letters and misses the requirement for thematic consistency.

questions.q: Does an acrostic poem require the lines to rhyme at the end?
questions.a: No, it does not. A wrong answer reveals a common misconception that all poems must rhyme, whereas acrostic poems focus on the vertical spelling constraint.

questions.q: Create a 4-line acrostic poem for the word "HOME."
questions.a: H-Happiness lives inside, O-Open doors for friends, M-Many memories made, E-Everything feels safe. A poor answer would lack a theme or fail to use the correct starting letters.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: An acrostic poem is a creative writing form where the first letter of each line, when read ______ from top to bottom, spells out a specific word or phrase related to the poem’s theme.
Fill in the blank: Have you ever tried to hide a secret message inside your ______?
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student will be able to construct an original acrostic poem of at least five lines where every line logically relates to the chosen subject word.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Have you ever tried to hide a secret ______ inside your writing?
